Learning notes: TradeHQ — Free Paper Trading Simulator

Practice simulated trading across 170 assets with $100,000 in virtual cash. No real money is involved. Learn order mechanics, portfolio tracking, and risk concepts across stocks, crypto, ETFs, forex and commodities.

Published by TradeHQ, created by Anuga Weerasinghe. Publisher background and editorial approach. No independent professional review is claimed; any recorded source-check scope appears on the page.

What TradeHQ actually is

TradeHQ is a free paper-trading simulator for people learning how markets work. Every account starts with $100,000 in virtual cash. Nothing on the site touches real money: there is no brokerage account, no deposit, no withdrawal and no order ever reaches an exchange. Supported holdings use periodically refreshed provider quotes. Unsupported assets can use fixed simulator prices, and charts may show synthetic practice candles. Price and chart labels explain their source and freshness.

A practice account lets you examine decisions without putting savings at risk. For example, compare how different quantities change a hypothetical loss, or record why you changed an exit plan. These exercises do not establish why most beginners lose money or guarantee that practice changes later behaviour.

What you can do here
Paper trade 170 instruments across stocks, crypto, ETFs, forex and commodities using market orders.
Track a full practice portfolio — open positions, realised and unrealised P&L, maximum drawdown, open-position P&L dispersion and allocation snapshots.
Work through four structured courses (options, futures, macro reading and trading psychology) with quizzes and completion badges.
Read a 49-term trading glossary written in plain language, each entry with a detailed explanation and a worked example.
Follow step-by-step guides for individual assets, side-by-side asset comparisons, and named strategy walkthroughs.
Keep a trading journal, build daily streaks with the daily challenge, and run a 30-day practice duel against a friend.
Who it is for, and who it is not for

TradeHQ is built for beginners and self-directed learners who want a place to rehearse market mechanics and a repeatable process without using real money. It can also be useful in classroom or independent-study settings.

It is not for you if you want signals, copy-trading, portfolio management, or someone to tell you what to buy. We do not publish price targets, we do not run a Discord with calls, and we do not accept payment for coverage of any asset. If you are looking for a recommendation, this is the wrong site.

How to start in five minutes
Open the markets page and pick one instrument you already recognise.
Read its guide page so you know what actually moves it before you trade it.
Choose a deliberately small practice position first, then compare how different simulated position sizes affect drawdown and volatility.
Write down, before you enter, where you would exit if you are wrong.
Come back the next day, review the trade in the journal, and repeat.
Why practice first, honestly

The argument for a simulator is not that practice guarantees profit — it does not. It is that the cost of learning market mechanics is unavoidable, and you get to choose whether you pay it in money or in time. A beginner can practice buying and selling holdings with virtual capital, then review those decisions without risking savings. TradeHQ currently supports market orders only; it does not simulate resting limit orders or short positions.

There is a real limitation to be honest about: a simulator removes the emotional weight of losing your own money, and that weight changes behaviour. Treat practice as the place to build a repeatable process — sizing, exits, journaling, review — and expect the emotional part to still be new when real money is involved.

Common questions
Is TradeHQ free? Yes, entirely. There is no paid tier, no trial and no card required.
Do I need an account? No. Practice trading, courses and the glossary work without signing up. An optional account supports profiles and community features. Account cash, positions and server-recorded trades restore across devices when available; earlier guest trade history and journals remain on the original browser, while signed-in lessons and journey progress can sync privately when online.
Is the money real? No. Every balance, order and result is simulated, and the platform holds no funds.
Are the prices real? Supported assets use periodically refreshed provider observations. Unsupported assets can use fixed simulator prices; charts may be synthetic. Check each source and timestamp rather than assuming a continuous exchange feed.
Does TradeHQ execute investments or provide personalized advice? No. Trading examples and educational indicator labels are illustrative, not personal recommendations, and the simulator places virtual orders only.
Where is my data? Guest practice records stay in your browser. Signed-in cash, positions and server-recorded trades are stored in Supabase and restored when the service is available. Guest trade history, journal entries and streaks remain browser-held; signed-in lessons and journey progress can sync privately. A badge count alone is not the complete course record.

About TradeHQ

TradeHQ exists to make financial education more accessible through practical learning. It is an educational simulator — not a brokerage, not an advisor.

Mission

Make financial literacy practical. TradeHQ lets anyone learn how markets work by doing — users manually place simulated market buys and sells, watch portfolios respond to news and price action, and study the outcomes without risking a single dollar.

Vision

A world where the first exposure to trading is educational, not expensive. Beginners should be able to make — and learn from — their first thousand mistakes on a simulator, not on their savings.

Educational Philosophy

Learning by doing beats learning by reading. Every feature — the $100,000 virtual portfolio, the educational mentor, the daily challenge, the wiki and the compound growth simulator — exists to turn abstract concepts (risk, position sizing, diversification, psychology) into things you can feel through hands-on practice.

Open the hypothetical compound growth calculator

Transparency

TradeHQ is not a brokerage. We do not custody funds, execute real trades, or provide financial advice. Prices shown are simulated or delayed and are for education only. Third-party advertising and optional analytics are described in the privacy policy; their operation depends on provider settings and applicable user choices.

Technology

TradeHQ is a modern web application built with React, TypeScript and a serverless backend. Guest practice records stay in your browser so you can start without signing up. Account cash, positions and server-recorded trades restore across devices when available; earlier guest trade history and journals remain browser-held; signed-in lessons and beginner-journey progress can sync privately when online. The standalone mentor uses a built-in answer library and local topic matching without an AI API request; portfolio mentor tools can use simulated portfolio context.

Creator

TradeHQ was created by Anuga Weerasinghe as an educational software project focused on helping beginners understand financial markets through simulation and structured learning.

What TradeHQ Is Not
Not a brokerage — no real orders are ever routed to any exchange.
Not a financial or investment advisor — nothing on the site is a recommendation to buy or sell.
Not a source of live, guaranteed market data — prices are simulated or delayed for education.
Not a substitute for professional advice — talk to a licensed advisor before investing real money.
How the material is written and reviewed

TradeHQ uses AI-assisted drafting and editing for educational material and software. Checks include worked-example arithmetic, consistency with simulator features and source suitability within the scope recorded on each page. These checks do not establish that every statement is correct or independently reviewed by a professional. References may provide background rather than evidence that a strategy predicts prices. Options and futures lessons are conceptual; the simulator does not execute those contracts.

Community Reviews publish visitor-submitted feedback; we do not independently verify reviewers' identities or experiences. The Community Practice Board publishes optional, server-recorded ranked simulated portfolios, with earlier browser-reported results labelled separately. These are not independently verified investment results. Neither feedback nor practice rankings promise real-world returns. Educational figures use cited sources or clearly labelled hypothetical examples; when a question has no honest answer — which asset will rise, whether a strategy will work for you — the page says so instead of guessing. Content is revised whenever a reader points out an error or a market mechanism changes, and corrections are made in place rather than quietly removed.

Who builds TradeHQ

TradeHQ is maintained as an independent educational project to help learners explore market mechanics with virtual balances. The simulator does not require or enable real-money trading.

TradeHQ is an educational simulator, not a brokerage or registered investment adviser. It does not accept funds or place real securities orders, and no exchange or brokerage affiliation is claimed.

How the content is produced
TradeHQ uses AI-assisted drafting and editing for educational material and software. Content is prepared for this site rather than syndicated; AI assistance does not establish accuracy or originality by itself.
Factual claims about market mechanics cite exchange, regulator or central-bank documentation where possible.
Illustrative chart-pattern labels, calculated indicators and hypothetical scenarios should not be interpreted as verified price forecasts or personalised instrument recommendations.
Errors are corrected when reported; the contact page is the fastest route.
How the project is funded

TradeHQ is free to use with no subscription and no paid tier. It is not funded by broker referrals or by payment for asset coverage, and no company pays to appear in a lesson, comparison or guide.

Why this site exists

Most people meet trading through advertising: a broker campaign, an influencer's screenshot, or an app that makes placing an order feel like a game. Almost none of that explains what an order actually does, what position sizing is, or how quickly leverage removes an account. TradeHQ exists to be the boring middle step between that advertising and someone's savings.

TradeHQ does not present practice results as evidence of future income. Community Reviews publish visitor-submitted feedback without independently verifying identity or experience. The Community Practice Board displays server-recorded ranked simulated portfolios, not verified investment returns.

Editorial standards
Education-first positioning: illustrations of market indicators or price scenarios do not constitute verified trade signals, profitable strategies or personal financial recommendations.
No invented statistics, testimonials, credentials or performance figures.
Numbers in lessons are worked examples and are labelled as such.
Every page states that the platform is educational and simulated.
Corrections are made promptly when a factual error is reported.
Contacting the maintainer
